narrative.northStar: The Phosphor Scope on an Ink Field
narrative.overview:
The two pages served by the Pi are WaveKit brand surfaces in the kit's dark theme (v1.0, vendored unchanged in `ui/brand/`). The page is a dark green-black ink field with paper-coloured text. One recessed well, the screen, carries the verdict, the headline rate and a scope of small multiples that all share one five-minute time base. Phosphor, the brand's signal colour, marks live measured signal and healthy state, and nothing else. Everything the operator might act on sits beside the screen as rows grouped by space. Developer detail sits open and quiet at the foot of the page.

The status page (`index.html`, served at `/`) answers one question first: are samples flowing from the dongle at the rate expected? The verdict answers in words. The rate gives the figure. The flow trace shows the last five minutes, and CPU, Memory, SoC temperature and Power dips are drawn underneath on the same time base, so a single cursor reads every channel at one moment. The first-boot setup page (`boot.html`, which loads `app.css` plus `boot.css`) uses the same nameplate and screen, cut down to a verdict, a three-step track and a clock.

The page is dark only. Every block is drawn from the first paint and readings swap text inside boxes of fixed size, so nothing moves as data arrives, changes or goes stale. These pages seed the WaveKit web dashboard's design language: the border policy, the no-jump principle, the mini-chart vocabulary and the measure rules carry over unchanged.
keyCharacteristics: Brand kit applied directly: vendored wordmark, favicon, D-DIN Condensed and Noto Sans, and the dark-theme colour values.
One ink field plus one recessed well (the screen). The only raised tone is surface: the endpoint field and the cursor readout.
Grouping by space, alignment and tone. A drawn line is kept only where it carries meaning.
Nothing moves when data changes. Every block exists from the first paint; readings swap text inside boxes of fixed size. The one allowed reflow is a client joining or leaving.
Phosphor means live, measured and healthy. Amber and red are semantic hues kept outside the brand palette.
Small multiples on one shared time base, read by one cursor; mini-charts only where they add a fact.
State is given by a word, and by a lamp or trace colour as well. Stale data dims and is never shown in a healthy colour.

rules.name: The Phosphor Means Live Rule
rules.body: Phosphor marks a fresh measurement or a healthy state. When the screen is not fresh (data-fresh="false"), traces and dips ticks are redrawn in paper-3 at 0.5 opacity, the phosphor wash is removed, and the rate falls back to paper-3. Rows, client slots and measurement sources say "Last known".

rules.name: The Verdict Colours the Trace Rule
rules.body: The flow trace, its wash and the rate take the screen's verdict hue: phosphor when ok, amber when warn, red when fault. A host channel recolours its own trace and value from its own state. A client's sparkline takes the client's state.

rules.name: The Focus Is Phosphor Rule
rules.body: Every focusable element gets a 2px phosphor outline with a 3px offset. On the scope the offset is 6px.

rules.name: The Numbers in Noto Rule
rules.body: Any figure that updates live is set in Noto Sans with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, which is set on the body. D-DIN never sets a live number.

rules.name: The Condensed Voice Rule
rules.body: Uppercase spaced D-DIN is used for short names only: the page name, section legends, channel and row names, the axis, step names, and button and contact words. It never sets a sentence or a measurement.

rules.name: The Darker Well Rule
rules.body: Depth goes down, never up. The screen is set into the field by tone alone. Nothing casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Still Page Rule
rules.body: Layout never shifts as data arrives, changes, goes stale or disappears, with one stated exception: the client list renders exactly as many rows as there are clients (capped at three, the last summarising the rest), so a client joining or leaving may reflow what follows. Per-poll value changes never may. Draw every block from the first paint; reserve lines instead of adding them (two verdict-detail lines, three below 560px; two-line rows; the rate's two lines); keep each client row a fixed height; swap content, never insert blocks; set changing text in fixed boxes (em-sized figure boxes, stretched right-set lines); keep poll-driven text to one line with an ellipsis safety net; let only static text wrap, where nothing follows it. Verified with a layout-shift observer and bounding-box comparison over a full /live/ loop at 1440, 1024 and 390 px: shifts only at client join/leave moments.

rules.name: The Line Must Mean Something Rule
rules.body: Group with spacing, alignment and tone. Keep a line only when it is data: minute lines and channel zeros on the scope, the flow's full scale, the dashed expected rate, the receiver-start marker, the cursor, lane and sparkline baselines, step bars. No outlines on panels, no rules under rows or legends, no rule between the endpoint field and its button.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Text takes the width of its column; a cap is added only where the column runs past a comfortable line (verdict detail 68ch, notes 80ch). text-wrap: balance for headings and short notes, pretty for detail sentences. Reserve the lines copy needs, then write copy to fit them. File names in prose never break at their hyphens.

rules.name: The Mini-chart Rule
rules.body: A small chart is drawn only where it adds a fact the words beside it do not: trace (time on the shared base), lane (event ticks), sparkline (a client's delivered rate as this page saw it, on the flow's full scale), meter (a share of a whole), bars (Wi-Fi). No axes or labels; the state hue colours the mark; stale marks dim; the figure always sits beside the chart.

dos: Do use the vendored wordmark SVG at 120px or wider, and keep the brand files in `ui/brand/` byte-identical to `packages/brand`.
Do set live figures in Noto Sans with tabular figures, in boxes that do not change size. D-DIN is for names and verdicts.
Do keep phosphor for live, healthy signal, and redraw stale data in paper-3 at half opacity.
Do put every trend on the one shared five-minute time base, so one cursor reads them all.
Do label a reference line or marker where it is drawn.
Do leave gaps in a trace blank. Smoothing never spans a missing sample.
Do reserve the space a state needs before the state arrives, and measure `/live/` for layout shift after any layout change.
Do group with space and tone first; add a line only when it is data.
Do keep developer detail (pids, counters, measurement sources) in Diagnostics, at the foot of the page.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, which turns off every animation and transition.
donts: Don't add a light theme, another typeface, or Barlow back.
Don't add shadows or outlines around panels. The well's darker tone is the only depth.
Don't use amber or red decoratively. They are semantic status hues and not part of the brand palette.
Don't show a stale, missing or unmeasurable value in phosphor or another healthy colour.
Don't split power into several indicators. It is one fact with a sub-line.
Don't insert or remove blocks when data changes (client rows joining or leaving are the one exception), hide a section until data arrives, or let a value wrap onto a new line on a poll.
Don't reintroduce tiles, annunciator windows, a stage lamp chain or an uncapped clients table. Host trends belong in the scope, facts in rows, clients in at most three rows.
Don't draw a chart that repeats its neighbour without adding a fact.
Don't use glyph or emoji icons. Lamps, bars, meters and the check are drawn in CSS or SVG.
